account:
Today I have mostly followed my ordinary appointments: office business, a market walk, lunch at home, and town accounts. The treasury contained 128 emeralds, which I left untouched. We have not located receipts or account ledgers; the secretary has no receipts prepared. That is unfinished business, not proof of wrongdoing.

The main activity reported in town concerns the baker. Several townsfolk said the baker carried wheat at the bakery. At 10:52 I saw the baker carrying a sack of bread, and at 11:00 I saw bread being put into the market stall chest. Townsfolk 08 and 28 also reported the baker carrying a sack of bread at the inn. This could simply be ordinary baking and deliveries. I do not yet know of any unusual gathering or what those deliveries were for beyond supplying bread.

The secretary has now confirmed my three o'clock tea with the neighbour at the east-bank cottage, road point (16, -60, 105). The innkeeper has also requested an appointment tomorrow at eighteen hundred in the great hall, specifically asking that I not arrive early. That timing condition is the most unusual detail I have heard. It might mean preparations or a private matter, but I have no evidence of its purpose or of who else is involved. I have told the secretary to confirm it and asked what the innkeeper wants to discuss. The secretary's latest reply repeats the request for approval, so I cannot yet be certain it has been recorded. My feeling that something is happening without me remains a suspicion, not an established fact.
